tasks.title: Add doctor's guidelines check: provenance on every rule, and a budget of 20
tasks.goal: A rule that cites no defect or intervention cannot be judged when it is time to prune, and too many rules has hurt before (L9). This task defines a rule and its provenance and adds a doctor check, printed right after `gate edits`, that counts the rules and warns past 20 or on a rule with no ID. Both are warnings: the operator decides what to retire, and no exit code changes.

references.why: P3–P5 are the proposals this brief implements and the seeds of the guidelines file; the task must not drift from them

acceptance: A rule is a line of .vloop/repo-guidelines.md starting `- ` at the left margin, in any section; a line inside an HTML comment (single- or multi-line) is not one. Provenance is a token D<8 digits>-<4 digits> or I<8 digits>-<4 digits>, optionally followed by the rest of the ID
doctor prints a check `guidelines` right after `gate edits`, in text and as the next entry in --json: no file `- guidelines`; within budget with provenance everywhere `✓ guidelines <n> rule(s)`

Over 20 rules: `! guidelines <n> rules, over the budget of 20 — retire or merge some before adding more`; rules without provenance: `! guidelines <k> rule(s) cite no defect or intervention: line <a>, line <b>` with 1-based line numbers; both: one warning line, the two messages joined by `; `, the second keeping its `guidelines` (e.g. `! guidelines 21 rules, over the budget of 20 — …; guidelines 2 rule(s) cite no defect or intervention: line 5, line 6`)
The budget is 20 and not configurable; both are warnings: no exit code changes and doctor writes nothing

tasks.title: Put the plugin skills on word budgets enforced by a test
tasks.goal: Skills grow by drift; L10 makes growth a recorded decision by a failing test. The test counts each plugin skill's whitespace-separated words, frontmatter included, against a ceiling that lives beside it with a comment saying when and why it was set. No gate may run the repository's tests, so the gate judges the counting through one function this plan pins, `Check(pluginDir string) []string` in package `internal/budget`, which it calls from its own oracle on synthetic skills; the committed test is the review's to rule on, and calls the same function on this repository's plugin/.

references.why: P3–P5 are the proposals this brief implements and the seeds of the guidelines file; the task must not drift from them

acceptance: Package internal/budget exports `func Check(pluginDir string) []string`: for each of the five skills, it counts the whitespace-separated words of `<pluginDir>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`, the whole file with its frontmatter, as wc -w counts them, and returns one message per skill over its ceiling, `<skill>: <count> words, over its ceiling of <ceiling>`, with thousands separators (e.g. `plan: 4,213 words, over its ceiling of 4,100`); a skill exactly at its ceiling is not reported
The ceilings are plan 4,100, gate-review 1,550, work 1,800, review 1,650, operate 1,750, each beside the test with one comment saying when and why it was last set

A committed Go test, outside cmd/, calls budget.Check on this repository's plugin/ and fails with each message it returns, and passes on the tree as this task leaves it. Violation: the budget shipped with no committed test the checks run, or a test that does not fail when a skill grows past its ceiling
Raising a ceiling is an edit of that comment and number. Violation: a ceiling raised, or a skill trimmed, to make room, beyond what L10 sets
The word counting is one function the metrics task (T10) can share, not a second copy

gate_history.reason: Gate review round 2 found pins-unnamed on internal/budget.Check; the seam is named in T9's acceptance, so a work session cannot build it elsewhere, and the round-1 alternative (running the committed test) is task-reach. Root cause: the brief's L10 makes the deliverable a test while forbidding gates that run tests. Gate kept, ruling recorded in it.
